slides.headline: October 12, 2014: a cyclone with 185 km/h winds hit India's coast. It killed 116 people - not tens of thousands.
Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Hudhud made landfall near Visakhapatnam at peak intensity
slides.body: With sustained winds near 185 km/h and gusts to 260 km/h, Hudhud was the first cyclone to cross the Visakhapatnam coast in October since 1985 - and by every historical measure, a storm of this strength should have killed far more people than it did.

slides.eyebrow: What actually kept the toll low
slides.headline: India moved roughly 400,000 people off the coast before the storm ever arrived.
slides.body: IMD forecasting and coordinated evacuation drills - built up since the 1999 Odisha super-cyclone killed nearly 10,000 people with far less warning - let authorities move almost half a million people out of Hudhud's path in time.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat measures disaster response in evacuations completed, not just damage counted.
slides.body: Fifteen decades after a cyclone with no warning system killed tens of thousands in Calcutta, a cyclone nearly as strong killed 116 - because the warning system finally existed.

sources.text: India Meteorological Department (RSMC New Delhi) - Cyclone Hudhud report
